title: API key is a string literal in client-side JavaScript
evidence: api.js is loaded by index.html:25 as a plain script. The key is sent as a Bearer token from the browser on every getOrders and refund call (api.js:6, api.js:11). Driven: the request to the API carries it from the page.
failing_case: Anyone who opens the page and views source, or the network tab, copies the key and can call GET /orders and POST /refunds directly, with no UI and no confirmation step.
remediation: Move the key to a server or proxy that authenticates the user and calls the API. Rotate this key, because it is already in the repo.

title: refund() never waits for the request and always reports ok: true
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await and discards the promise. api.js:12 returns ok:true at once. app.js:51 shows 'Refunded N orders!' on r.ok. Driven with the refunds endpoint answering HTTP 500: the toast read 'Refunded 2 orders!' and no error was shown.
failing_case: Select two orders, click Refund selected while the API returns 500 or the network is down. The user sees 'Refunded 2 orders!' and nothing was refunded. A rejected fetch also becomes an unhandled rejection. Double-clicking sends two refund POSTs, because nothing is disabled while one is in flight.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return or throw the real outcome with the server's reason, show failure in the UI, disable the button while pending, and send an idempotency key.

title: Selection list only ever grows: unchecking does not remove, duplicates and old ids are refunded
evidence: The handler pushes on check and never removes on uncheck. selected is never cleared on a page change, on a new search or after a refund. renderTable rebuilds the rows unchecked, so the screen no longer shows what selected holds. Driven: check order 11, check 12, uncheck 11, click refund: the POST body was {"ids":["11","12"]}.
failing_case: The user ticks order 11, changes their mind and unticks it, then clicks Refund selected. Order 11 is refunded anyway. Ticking and unticking the same box twice sends the id twice. Ids from a previous page or search stay in the list and are refunded with no checkbox showing them.
remediation: Keep selection as a Set keyed by id, add and delete on change, re-apply checked state when rendering, clear it after a successful refund, and show the count next to the button.

title: The Refund button is a span: no keyboard access, no role, no focus
evidence: A span has no tab stop and no button role. Driven: pressing Tab from the status select moved focus to the first row checkbox, skipping Refund selected. Enter and Space do nothing on a span. WCAG 2.1.1 (A) and 4.1.2 (A).
failing_case: A keyboard or screen reader user can select orders but can never refund them. The page's main action is unreachable.
remediation: Use <button type="button" class="refund">, which gives focus, Enter and Space and the role for free.

title: Customer name and id are written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: o.customer.name and o.id come from the API and go straight into an HTML template (app.js:32). Traced: a name of becomes a live element in the table on the page where it falls. The rendered row HTML was confirmed to be built by raw interpolation.
failing_case: A customer registers as . When any staff member views that page of orders, the script runs in the dashboard origin, with access to whatever the page can reach, including the refund action.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent (or escape every interpolated value), set data-id through dataset, and build the rows once instead of with innerHTML +=.

quote: **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the API key never leaves the server; it is shipped to every browser
evidence: api.js:3 holds the key and api.js:6 and api.js:11 send it from the browser. Driven.
failing_case: A reader trusts the README and deploys the page as is; the key is public.
remediation: Fix the code (proxy the API on a server), then keep the sentence; until then delete it.

quote: 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing example is wrong: 12 seats at $15 with 20% off is $1,728 a year, or $144 if $15 is the yearly price
evidence: Recomputed: 12 seats x $15 x 12 months = $2,160; less 20% = $1,728. If $15 is per seat per year, 12 x $15 x 0.8 = $144. $1,440 matches neither; it equals 12 seats x $15 x 10 months x 0.8.
failing_case: A customer budgets $1,440 and is billed $1,728, or the reverse.
remediation: State whether the $15 is monthly, then correct the total ($1,728 a year if monthly) and name the formula.

title: Empty result shows $NaN as the average order; an error response or a missing customer crashes the stats
evidence: Divides by orders.length with no guard. Driven: a search returning [] rendered 'REVENUE $0.00, ORDERS 0, AVG ORDER $NaN'. o.customer.tier (app.js:13) throws if customer is null, and for...of throws if the API returns an error object instead of an array.
failing_case: Type a search that matches nobody. The AVG ORDER card reads $NaN. The average also divides net revenue (paid minus refunded) by all orders, including refunded and pending, so it is not an average order value.
remediation: Guard the empty case (show an em dash), define the average over the intended set of orders, and validate the response shape before rendering.

title: Pagination is off by one: page 1 starts at the 11th order, the first 10 are unreachable
evidence: page starts at 1 (app.js:3) and the offset is page * PAGE_SIZE, so page 1 shows orders[10..19]. Driven with 25 orders: the first row on load was Cust11, and Prev cannot reach orders 1 to 10 until page 0 is reached via a negative page.
failing_case: Load the dashboard with 25 orders. Page 1 shows orders 11 to 20. Orders 1 to 10, normally the newest, are never shown.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, or make page zero-based and display page + 1.

title: Refund fires on one click with no confirmation, and with an empty selection
evidence: The handler calls refund(selected) directly. No confirm step, no check that selected is non-empty. README.md:9 states refunds are confirmed before they are sent. Driven: one click sent the POST.
failing_case: A mis-click on Refund selected sends the refund at once. With nothing selected it posts {"ids":[]} and shows 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
remediation: Show a confirm dialog that names the number of orders and the total amount, disable the action when nothing is selected, and say 'Refund 3 orders ($412.00)' on the button.

title: Text contrast is far below 4.5:1 on the stat labels, the header eyebrow and the pager buttons
evidence: Computed: .lbl #aaa on #fff is 2.32:1 (styles.css:9); .eyebrow #c7c2f0 on the #6366f1 to #8b5cf6 gradient is 2.50 to 2.64:1 (styles.css:4); button #aaa on the #F4F1EA page background is 2.06:1 (styles.css:18). All three are at 11 to 12 px. WCAG 1.4.3 (AA).
failing_case: REVENUE / ORDERS / AVG ORDER labels and the Prev / Next buttons are hard to read for low-vision users and in daylight.
remediation: Use a colour of at least 4.5:1 for each (for example #595959 on white and on #F4F1EA, #fff on a darker header), and a size of 12 px or more.

title: Table has a fixed 1000 px width and the stats are always 3 columns: the page scrolls sideways on a phone
evidence: Driven at 390 px viewport width: document scrollWidth was 1024. styles.css:6 forces repeat(3, 1fr) with no breakpoint. td:nth-child(2) is capped at 120 px with overflow hidden (styles.css:15), which clips names with no ellipsis. WCAG 1.4.10 (AA).
failing_case: On a 390 px phone the user must scroll horizontally to see the Status column, and long customer names are cut off with no way to read them.
remediation: Use width: 100% with a wrapper that has overflow-x: auto or a stacked layout under 640 px, a one-column stats grid on small screens, and text-overflow: ellipsis plus a title on the name.

quote: **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README claims full WCAG 2.1 AA conformance that the code fails, and mislabels 2.5.5 as AA
evidence: See findings on the span button (index.html:19), the removed focus outline (styles.css:19), contrast 2.06 to 2.64:1 (styles.css:9), missing labels, color-only status and sideways scroll at 390 px. Criterion 2.5.5 is Level AAA in WCAG 2.1, not AA. Touch targets are about 18 px (styles.css:18).
failing_case: A buyer or a procurement team relies on the AA claim and ships the tool to staff who use a keyboard or screen reader. They cannot refund an order.
remediation: Remove the claim until it is audited and fixed, or state the measured conformance and the known gaps, and cite 2.5.5 as AAA.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured dot with no text
evidence: The dot is an empty span coloured green, red or yellow (styles.css:17), with no text and no title. The red and green pair is also hard to tell apart for red-green colour blindness. WCAG 1.4.1 (A), 1.1.1 (A).
failing_case: A colour-blind user cannot tell paid from refunded, and a screen reader user hears nothing in the Status column.
remediation: Render the status word inside the cell (with a dot as decoration if wanted), or add a visually hidden text.

title: Every keystroke fires an unthrottled request and responses are applied in arrival order
evidence: load() (app.js:38) reads the inputs, awaits getOrders and then assigns orders and renders. There is no debounce, no abort and no check that the response matches the current input. Traced.
failing_case: The user types 'ab'. The request for 'a' is slow and the request for 'ab' is fast. 'ab' results render first, then 'a' arrives and overwrites them. The search box says 'ab' and the table shows results for 'a'. Selecting the status filter during a pending request has the same problem.
remediation: Debounce input by about 250 ms, hold an AbortController (or a sequence number) and ignore any response that is not the latest.

title: Search box, status filter and row checkboxes have no accessible name; the first header cell is empty
evidence: No <label> or aria-label on #q (a placeholder is not a label), on the #status select (index.html:18), or on the generated row checkboxes (app.js:32). The first th is empty (index.html:21). WCAG 1.3.1 and 3.3.2 (A), 4.1.2 (A).
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'combo box' with no purpose, and each checkbox as 'checkbox' with no customer. The user can't tell which order they are ticking.
remediation: Add visible labels (or aria-label) for search and status, aria-label="Select order {id} for {name}" on each checkbox, and a visually hidden 'Select' header.

title: Focus outline is removed from buttons, inputs and selects with no replacement
evidence: No :focus-visible style exists anywhere in styles.css. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA).
failing_case: A keyboard user tabbing through Prev, Next, the search box and the status filter cannot see where focus is.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px } on all controls.

title: Page count rounds down: the last partial page is not counted, and 0 orders shows 'of 0'
evidence: Math.floor(25 / 10) is 2 but 25 orders need 3 pages. Driven: label read 'Page 1 of 2' with 25 orders.
failing_case: With 25 orders the label says there are 2 pages and the last 5 orders are not counted. With 9 orders it says 'of 0'.
remediation: Use Math.max(1, Math.ceil(orders.length / PAGE_SIZE)).

title: A failed or non-JSON load is unhandled: no error message, stale data stays, nothing says loading
evidence: No try/catch around the await, api.js:7 never checks res.ok, and there is no loading or empty state in index.html. Driven with the API unreachable: console 'pageerror Failed to fetch', the page stayed blank with no message.
failing_case: The API returns 503 with an HTML or JSON error body, or the network drops. The user sees an empty page or the previous results, with no hint that the data is stale or why.
remediation: Check res.ok in getOrders and throw with the status, catch in load(), show an inline error with a Retry button, and add loading and 'No orders match' states.

title: Prev and Next have no bounds, and a new search does not reset the page
evidence: Neither handler clamps page, and the buttons are never disabled. load() (app.js:38) does not reset page. Driven with 25 orders: three Prev clicks showed 'Page -2 of 2' with 10 rows, and five Next clicks showed 'Page 3 of 2' with an empty table.
failing_case: On page 3 the user types a search that returns 4 results. The table is empty, with no explanation, because page is still 3.
remediation: Clamp page to [1, pageCount], disable Prev and Next at the ends, and set page = 1 whenever the query or status changes.

title: Search text is put into the URL without encoding
evidence: query comes straight from the input box into the query string. Driven: the URL carried q=zzz verbatim; any '&', '#' or '+' changes its meaning. Traced.
failing_case: Searching for 'R&D Ltd' sends q=R and an extra parameter D Ltd. Searching 'a#b' drops everything after '#'. A user can add `&status=refunded` to override the filter.
remediation: Build the URL with URLSearchParams, or wrap each value in encodeURIComponent.

title: Pricing rules (gold discount, 8.25% tax, refund sign) are hard-coded inside a render function
evidence: renderStats (app.js:8) computes discount, tax and revenue inline with magic numbers 0.9 and 1.0825, and writes to the DOM in the same function. The table at app.js:32 shows the raw o.total while the stats apply tax and discount, so the two displays of the same order disagree.
failing_case: A gold order with total 100 shows $100 in the table and contributes $97.43 to revenue. Changing the tax rate means editing view code, with no test for the rule.
remediation: Move the calculation to one pure, tested function (or use the server's figures); the view only displays the result.

title: The result toast is not a live region and never goes away
evidence: No role="status" or aria-live on #toast, so screen readers do not announce it (WCAG 4.1.3, AA). app.js:51 only ever sets display:block; there is no hide, and the text is not cleared by the next action.
failing_case: After a refund, a blind user hears nothing. Sighted users see 'Refunded 2 orders!' stay on screen indefinitely, even after they select other orders.
remediation: Add role="status" (role="alert" for failures), set text and hide it after a delay or on a close button.

quote: button { border: 0; background: none; color: #aaa; padding: 2px 4px; font-size: 12px; }
title: Prev and Next are 12 px text buttons with 2 px padding: tiny targets and no visible button shape
evidence: Height is roughly 18 px, with no border or fill. Row checkboxes use the browser default of about 13 px. This is below the 24 px of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 and nowhere near the 44 px that README.md:5 claims. (2.5.5 is Level AAA in 2.1.)
failing_case: On a touch screen the user often misses Prev and Next or taps the wrong row checkbox.
remediation: Give the pager buttons a visible border and a min-height of 44 px and padding of 8px 16px, and enlarge the checkbox hit area with a label.

title: The toast pulses forever and there is no prefers-reduced-motion rule
evidence: pop runs 'infinite alternate' with no pause, and styles.css has no @media (prefers-reduced-motion) block. Moving content that lasts more than 5 s needs a way to stop it: WCAG 2.2.2 (A).
failing_case: The toast scales 1 to 1.05 without end while it is on screen, which distracts and is hard on people with vestibular or attention conditions.
remediation: Remove the infinite animation (or run it once for about 200 ms) and wrap any motion in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

title: Performance claim has no measurement behind it
evidence: Every keystroke fetches the whole order list (app.js:45) and renderStats walks all orders (app.js:11); the table builds 10 rows with innerHTML += (app.js:32). No benchmark or test exists in the payload. 'Instantly' is not a figure.
failing_case: A reader expects 10,000 orders to render and update in real time with no debounce; unmeasured.
remediation: Measure it (time to first paint and per-keystroke cost at 10,000 rows) and state the number, or remove the claim.
